clue.text: "Thyrza"writer's name US soldiers chant

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers, plural GIS
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: Someone reports the name of a novelist being chanted by American troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name' is a link: the writer's name is what the wordplay spells. George Gissing wrote the novel Thyrza (1887).
explanation.definitionFit: George Gissing, the Victorian novelist, published Thyrza in 1887.

clue.text: Grand artist, bad actor, and Edinburgh's top novelist

parts.note: G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a ham is an overacting performer

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grand painter, a hammy performer and Edinburgh's leading writer gather.
explanation.walkthrough: Kenneth Grahame, author of The Wind in the Willows, was born in Edinburgh, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Grahame wrote The Wind in the Willows, a classic of English fiction.

clue.text: TV programme's job to appear daily without trouble

parts.note: a situation is a post or job
to come is to appear or arrive

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the trouble's letters are removed from the word daily

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, an ailment

explanation.surface: A television job requires turning up every day without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes AIL out of DAILY, leaving DY. 'programme's' is the programme plus 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a television genre built around a fixed set of characters in recurring scenarios.

clue.text: One book backs Du Maurier's Peter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to back a horse is to bet on it

explanation.surface: A single book supports the work of the novelist du Maurier.
explanation.walkthrough: George du Maurier's 1891 novel is Peter Ibbetson; 'Du Maurier' is not Daphne. The wordplay spells the name with E.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Ibbetson is the dreaming hero of George du Maurier's first novel.

clue.text: Moral of hapless play by Stoppard

indicators.note: read as hap-less, the play title loses its first three letters

parts.note: Hapgood is Tom Stoppard's 1988 spy play

explanation.surface: Someone draws a lesson from an unlucky Stoppard drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hapless' looks like 'unlucky' but splits as HAP-less: take HAP from Stoppard's Hapgood.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral as an adjective means virtuous, righteous.

clue.text: Class on vacation round Australia with Buddhist school's "Cock Pit" author

indicators.note: the emptied word sits round the other pieces, holding them inside
a word on vacation is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: OZ is the informal name for Australia
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A class empties for the holidays and travels around Australia with a Zen author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties 'Class' to its first and last letters, which sit 'round' the rest. James Gould Cozzens wrote the novel Cock Pit (1928).
explanation.definitionFit: James Gould Cozzens, the American novelist, wrote Cock Pit early in his career.

clue.text: Putting an end to Wallander suffering by the sound of it

indicators.note: the words are heard spoken, so the spelling may differ

parts.note: Kurt Wallander is Henning Mankell's detective; suffering is ailing

explanation.surface: A Swedish detective's ordeal brings his story to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtailing is cutting short or stopping something.

clue.text: Life left no time for Balak's father

parts.note: zip is liveliness, life

indicators.note: no means without, so the time letter is dropped from the word for left

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone loses vitality and runs out of time for an old king's parent.
explanation.walkthrough: In Numbers, Balak king of Moab is called the son of Zippor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Numbers names Zippor as the parent of Balak, king of Moab.

clue.text: Whose Christmas present revealed Ignorance?

parts.note: not a gift but the Ghost of Christmas Present in Dickens, who shows the miser two children, Ignorance and Want

explanation.surface: Someone opens a gift that turns out to expose their own ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: In A Christmas Carol the Ghost of Christmas Present uncovers the children Ignorance and Want for Dickens's miser.

clue.text: Her story may be described in Daniel as Annus Mirabilis

definitions.text: Her story may be described in Daniel

indicators.note: Latin for wonderful or strange, so the letters before it are wondrously transformed

explanation.surface: A year of wonders is recorded in the Book of Daniel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mirabilis' anagrams AS ANNUS. Susanna and the Elders is an addition to Daniel in the Apocrypha.
explanation.definitionFit: The tale of Susanna and the Elders is an apocryphal chapter of the Book of Daniel.

clue.text: Writers whose lives are their work

definitions.text: Writers whose lives are their work

parts.words: Writers whose lives are their work
parts.note: read literally: authors whose subject matter is their own life story, not people consumed by their jobs

explanation.surface: Workaholic authors live for nothing but their writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes the story of their own life makes that life the substance of the book.

clue.text: He gave us "Buck" as initial stake

parts.note: in poker the ante is the stake put in before the deal

explanation.surface: A gambler's opening bet is a dollar, a buck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' looks like slang for a dollar beside 'stake', but it is the title of a memoir by M. K. Asante.
explanation.definitionFit: The American writer M. K. Asante published the memoir Buck in 2013.

clue.text: Northern staff securing a working farm animal

parts.note: a staff is a pole
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A northern farmer leans on a stick while working the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' links the staff to the A it holds in front. Napoleon is the ruling pig in Orwell's Animal Farm, so 'farm animal' is a sly definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon is the pig who seizes power in Orwell's Animal Farm, literally an animal of that farm.

clue.text: Coat turned up at the front, revealing a device that shot John Wick

parts.note: a film is a thin coat or layer
turned up means arrived, came

indicators.note: at the front means only the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A coat that has been folded upward at the front exposes something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' is the film sense: John Wick was filmed, not gunned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera loaded with celluloid recorded the action movie, as a cinematographer shoots a feature.

clue.text: Revise tests about current leaders

parts.note: to revise a text is to edit it

indicators.note: the tests are wrapped about the current, holding it inside

parts.note: orals are spoken examinations
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone revises exams concerning those who lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks like people at the top, but in British newspapers a leader is an editorial.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leading article, the paper's own opinion piece, is called a leader.

clue.text: The fifth time Elizabeth von Arnim told this story

definitions.text: Elizabeth von Arnim told this story

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A novelist tells the same tale over again for the fifth time.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth von Arnim's 1921 novel bears this title, so it is the tale she told.

clue.text: Writer of The Front Page, The Bench, Psycho

indicators.note: psycho means deranged, so the letters are scrambled madly

explanation.surface: A list of film titles, a newspaper drama, a courtroom one and Hitchcock's thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Psycho' looks like another title, but it is the anagram signal on THE BENCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Hecht co-wrote the newspaper comedy The Front Page with Charles MacArthur.

clue.text: Scandinavian fisherman in "The Silver Darlings"

definitions.meaning: a native of Finland, a Nordic country
Neil Gunn's novel of herring fishing follows the boy and fisherman of this name

explanation.definitionFit: A Nordic person from Finland, and also the name of the young herring fisherman in Neil Gunn's novel.

clue.text: Italian author that is taken in by hoax Oscar

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the abbreviation goes into the hoax

parts.note: to fool is to hoax
SC (scilicet) means namely, that is
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An Italian writer is duped by a fake film award.
explanation.walkthrough: SC, short for Latin scilicet, is a convention for 'that is'; 'taken in' looks like 'deceived', but it means placed inside. Ugo Foscolo wrote Last Letters of Jacopo Ortis.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugo Foscolo was an Italian poet and novelist of the Napoleonic era.

clue.text: One helps a writer issue a Mann novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A publisher brings out a new book by Thomas Mann.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun after the author Mann, but it is the anagram signal on ISSUE A MANN.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretary who takes dictation or copies manuscripts is an assistant to an author.

clue.text: Hannay or a similar part elevated a US dramatist

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevated means read upwards, back to front
only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Buchan's hero Hannay, or some such character, raises an American playwright up.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Hannay is John Buchan's adventure hero. William Saroyan wrote The Time of Your Life.
explanation.definitionFit: William Saroyan was an Armenian-American playwright who won a Pulitzer for The Time of Your Life.

clue.text: Brief rest from an uprising in Tom Pocock originally

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: in a down entry, uprising means the word reads upwards, backwards
originally means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An account of a rebellion in the work of the historian Tom Pocock.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short sleep, a snooze.

clue.text: Maybe Arthur Gordon Pym contrived two ways to pen an article

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the rearranged letters hold the article inside
something contrived is artificially arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A character in a story devises two routes to write a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges TWO WAYS into STOWWAY; 'to pen' puts A inside. Poe's Arthur Gordon Pym begins his voyage hidden aboard a whaler.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's hero Pym sails hidden in the hold of the Grampus, a secret passenger; 'Maybe' marks him as an example.

clue.text: Rage harboured by quiet resistance who chronicled the Third Reich

indicators.note: harboured by means held inside, so the rage goes within the other pieces

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: Anger lurks within a silent wartime resistance movement in Nazi Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: William L. Shirer wrote The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich, the classic history of Nazi Germany.

clue.text: Zhivago's love of the sea after a revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns the sea's name round so it reads backwards

parts.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia

explanation.surface: Doctor Zhivago's beloved lies beyond a sea after the Russian Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests Pasternak's Russia, but it reverses ARAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lara Antipova is Yuri Zhivago's beloved in Pasternak's novel.

clue.text: Greek music hall host introducing style to sacred poem

parts.note: an odeon (odeion) was a roofed hall for music in ancient Greece

indicators.note: the host has the style introduced into him, so it goes inside

parts.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event
elan is flair or style
holy means sacred

explanation.surface: The compere at a Greek concert hall brings flair to a religious verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacred poem' looks like one phrase, but 'sacred' gives HOLY and 'poem' alone defines Keats's ode.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's 1819 ode is among the best-known lyric works in English verse.

clue.text: Location of a Phidias statue and a Manet painting

definitions.meaning: Phidias made the great statue of Zeus at the sanctuary in Elis, one of the ancient wonders
Manet's 1863 nude of a courtesan reclining, shown at the Salon of 1865

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek sanctuary housed Phidias's Zeus, and Manet gave the same name to his famous nude.

clue.text: Play, one modelled on a hero that's torn apart

parts.note: a play is divided into acts

indicators.note: modelled means shaped anew, so the letters are given a new form

explanation.surface: An actor in a play is cast as a tragic hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelled' rearranges ONE and A into AEON; 'on' is a link. Actaeon saw Artemis bathing and was turned into a stag and torn apart by his own hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the hunter who glimpsed Artemis bathing was changed into a stag and killed by his hounds.
